chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Muhammad, his son: 'O my son! How much remains with you from those expenses?' He said, 'Forty dinars.' He said: 'Bring it out and give charity with it.' He said, 'Nothing else remains with me other than it.' He said: 'Give charity with it, for God Mighty and Majestic will replace it. Do you not know that for everything there is a key, and the key to provision is charity? So give charity with it.'

So he did it, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had not waited ten days before four thousand dinars came to him from a source. Then he said: 'O my son! We gave forty dinars to God, and God gave us four thousand dinars.'

key_terms.الرِّزْق: al-rizq — divinely apportioned sustenance, provision from God
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: al-sadaqa — voluntary charitable giving, beyond obligatory zakat
key_terms.النَّفَقَة: nafaqa — expenses or provision set aside for household use
key_terms.مِفْتَاحُ الرِّزْقِ: miftah al-rizq — the key to sustenance/provision
key_terms.يُخْلِفُهَا: yakhlifuha — God will replace/restore what is given away in charity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say is the key to provision and sustenance?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts how Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructed his son Muhammad to give their last 40 dinars in charity, teaching that charity is the key to divine provision (rizq). Despite his son's hesitation, the Imam insisted, citing the principle that God replaces what is given in His path. Within ten days, 4000 dinars arrived — a hundredfold return — dramatically illustrating this teaching. The hadith was transmitted through Harun ibn Isa, who witnessed or heard this personal exchange between the Imam and his son, lending it an intimate biographical quality.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ali Bin Wahbaan, from his uncle Haroun Bin Isa who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Muhammad, his<sup>asws</sup> son: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! How much excess is there with you from those expenses?’ He said, ‘Forty Dinars’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Bring it out and give charity with it’. He said, ‘There does not remain with me anything apart from it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give in charity with it, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Replace it. But, do you not know that for everything there is a key, and a key for the sustenance is the charity, therefore give charity with it’.

So he did it and Abu Abdullah<sup>azwj</sup> did not remain for more than ten days before there came to him from a place, four thousand Dinars. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! We gave Allah<sup>azwj</sup> forty Dinars, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Gave us four thousand Dinars’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Wahban from his uncle, Harun ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to his son, Muhammad, ‘Son, how much is left with you of that (money) for expenses?’ He replied, ‘Forty dinars are left.’ He said, ‘You should go out and give it away as charity.’ The son said, ‘No more money is left with me besides this.’ The Imam said, ‘You should give it as charity, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, will replace it. Have you not noted that for everything there is a key, and the key to greater means of sustenance is giving charity, so give it as charity.’

The son followed the instruction. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, waited for only ten days until he received four thousand dinars from a certain place. He then said, ‘Son, we gave Allah forty dinars and He has given us four thousand dinars.’”
